newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Feb 18.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
* Freeport-McMoran Copper & Gold's ties to the Indonesian government helped it and Bre-X Minerals to win the Indonesian government's approval to mine the huge Busan gold find in Borneo.
* HealthSouth is negotiating to buy Horizon/CMS Healthcare for about $1 billion in stock, according to people familiar with the talks.

* One man's effort to sue the attorneys in a class-action lawsuit in which he paid more in legal fees than he won in settlement has gained support from nine state attorneys general, and a dozen others are expected to back the man's petition to get the case heard by the Supreme Court.
* The global telecommunications pact signed by negotiators at the World Trade Organization will favor growing giants with powerful alliances rather than lone entrepreneurs.

* Be Inc, a start-up developing a new personal computer operating system, plans to announce that its system will be included in Motorola's Macintosh-compatible computers. It is close to a similar pact with IBM.
* CompuServe said chief executive Robert Massey has resigned.
* Copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka pleaded guilty to charges of fraud and forgery in the $2.6 billion trading scandal at Sumitomo Corp.
* A new study supports the belief that younger mutual fund managers have better performing funds. -- Market Place column.
* Walt Disney's and CBS' interest in Starwave and Sportsline USA could be a prelude for both Internet start-ups to go public later this year.

* General Motors is becoming more active in public policy issues and its Washington, D.C. office has increased its lobbying efforts as the company builds new plants overseas and as the rising dollar propels GM's sales of foreign cars.
* A GM supplier reached a tentative pact with the United Automobile Workers union, averting a strike that would have shut down GM's 11 North American light truck plants.
* Caribbean officials are trying to lessen their dependence on American Airlines after the threat of a strike by the carrier's pilots.
* Wal-Mart will get its first unionized store following a decision by an Ontario government panel.
* The new owner of the nation's biggest book show, a unit of Reed-Elsevier, will announce that the publishers trade association has agreed to co-sponsor the convention.
